# LLMReady

> An open-source AI compatibility auditor. It classifies a site into one of six profiles, then validates /llms.txt, RFC 9309 robots.txt policy, static HTML signal-to-noise and the schema.org types that profile expects, returning the exact source line and a copy-paste fix for every miss.

LLMReady runs against the initial HTML response. It does not execute JavaScript against the target and does not store audits in a database. The public instance is free, open source and has no signup.

## The pipeline

1. **Raw site.** Fetch the initial HTML, `/llms.txt`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/openapi.json` and structured data without rendering.
2. **Site classification.** Hostname, sitemap and navigation paths, JSON-LD types, `og:type`, title/description copy, markup shape and the `llms.txt` index vote for one of six profiles: `saas`, `portfolio`, `docs`, `ecommerce`, `local-business` or `blog-media`. The winning profile and its top signals are returned in `classification`.
3. **Site AI compatibility.** The profile sets the expected schema types and whether OpenAPI is scored, then the four-pillar audit produces the score and fix queue. A manual override is available in the workspace or with `type=` on the API.

## What the audit measures

### Discovery & manifests

- `/llms.txt` is fetched as plain text and validated for one H1, a blockquote summary, H2 sections, a markdown link index and pagination markers.
- `/llms-full.txt` is treated as an optional single-request context bundle. It must be plain text, usable and unpaginated.
- `/sitemap.xml` is parsed, including sitemap indexes, and must contain URLs. The audit also checks for a `Sitemap:` directive in `robots.txt`.

### Crawler access

RFC 9309 matching is implemented directly: the longest matching path wins, `Allow` wins ties, and both `*` and `$` syntax are supported. The audit evaluates `GPTBot` (OpenAI), `ClaudeBot` (Anthropic), `Google-Extended` (Google), `PerplexityBot` (Perplexity) and `Bytespider` (ByteDance). It also checks for an explicit named AI policy, `robots` meta directives and a blocking `X-Robots-Tag` response header.

### Static parseability

- Exactly one H1 in the content region.
- Heading sequence without skipped levels.
- Static HTML signal-to-noise ratio of at least 65 percent of visible text. Content text is measured against navigation, header, footer, aside, banner, consent-widget and `aria-hidden` text.
- At least 600 characters of readable text in the initial HTML response.

Content is read from `main`, else `[role="main"]`, else the richest `article`, else `body`. A region that only holds a teaser falls back to the full document. Scripts, styles, SVGs, forms, frames and hidden nodes are removed before measurement.

### Structured data

- JSON-LD blocks are parsed and checked for `@context` and `@type`.
- The audit looks for one of the profile's expected types: `SoftwareApplication` for SaaS, `Person` for portfolios, `TechArticle` for docs, `Product` for e-commerce, `LocalBusiness` for local businesses and `Article` or `NewsArticle` for media.
- `/openapi.json`, `/.well-known/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml` are probed for OpenAPI documents. OpenAPI is scored for SaaS and docs profiles only.
- `/.well-known/security.txt` and `/.well-known/ai-plugin.json` are checked as optional discovery surfaces.

## Scoring

Each check returns pass, warn or fail, worth 100, 50 or 0 points. A pillar score is the weighted average of its checks. The overall score is the mean of the four pillars: discovery, access, parseability and structured data. Grades are A (90-100), B (75-89), C (60-74), D (40-59) and F (0-39).

## Workspace

The audit matrix shows the detected site profile, confidence and signals above every tab. Changing the override re-runs the audit against that profile. The matrix itself shows every check with its protocol, source file, exact line number, a short observation and an expandable code fix. The `llms.txt` editor builds both the manifest and the full bundle from the pages discovered during the audit, validates the result and offers copy and download actions. The scraper simulator shows the raw HTML beside the cleaned markdown a non-JS crawler would ingest, with payload reduction and token estimates.

## API

`GET /api/audit?url=example.com` returns a JSON report with:

- `classification` with the effective `type`, `confidence`, `method`, `detected` profile, `alternatives` ranked by support, top `signals` and `compatibility` rules.
- `score`, `grade`, `gradeLabel` and four `pillars`.
- Each check with `id`, `label`, `status`, `summary`, `detail`, `protocol`, `weight`, `evidence` and an optional `fix`.
- `evidence.file`, `evidence.line` and `evidence.snippet` for line-level evidence.
- `fix.language` and `fix.code` for a copy-paste resolution.
- `profile`, `pages`, `files`, `vision`, `fixes` and `meta`.

A bare domain or a full URL is accepted. Add `type=docs` (or `saas`, `portfolio`, `ecommerce`, `local-business`, `blog-media`) to pin the profile. Errors use `{ "error": { "code", "message", "hint?" } }`. Identical URLs are cached for five minutes per server instance, separately for each profile. The public rate limit is 30 audits per minute per IP.

## CLI and CI

The same audit engine is packaged for terminals and CI, so a local run and a pull request check return the same score and fixes.

- Install: clone the repository, run `pnpm install` and `pnpm build:cli`, then run `pnpm cli example.com` from the repository root. The bundle also runs directly with `node packages/cli/dist/index.js`.
- CLI: `llm-seo-toolbox example.com --min-score 75 --min-grade B`. Formats are `table` (default), `json`, `markdown` and `summary`; `--output` writes to a file. Exit code 0 means the threshold passed, 1 means the audit completed below a threshold and 2 means the audit could not run.
- Configuration: the CLI discovers `llm-seo-toolbox.config.json`, `.llmseotoolboxrc` or `.llmseotoolboxrc.json` in the working directory. CLI flags override file values.
- GitHub Action: build the bundle with `pnpm build:action`, then use `./actions/audit` in the workflow. The action audits the target URL, writes the report to the job summary, creates or updates one sticky pull request comment and fails the job when the configured score or grade is missed. Inputs are `url`, `min-score`, `min-grade`, `site-type`, `comment-on-pr`, `github-token` and `timeout`; outputs are `score`, `grade`, `passed` and `report-json`.
- Packages: `@llm-seo-toolbox/core` contains the classifier, four-pillar analyzer, scoring and report renderers. The Next.js workspace, `@llm-seo-toolbox/cli` and `@llm-seo-toolbox/action` all consume it.

## Standards and source

- llms.txt specification: https://llmstxt.org/
- RFC 9309: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309
- schema.org: https://schema.org/
- Source code: https://github.com/ABradwell/llm-seo-toolbox
- License: GPL-3.0-only
